title: StochasticSurjectiveInequalities.lean

problem_class.label: nonconvex
problem_class.details: Minimize a differentiable, possibly nonconvex objective f over c(x) ≤ 0; the differentiable constraint components may also be nonconvex.

oracle.label: stochastic_gradient
oracle.details: Unbiased estimates of ∇f(x) and the full constraint Jacobian J(x). Each oracle call evaluates both requested points using the same sample; samples across calls are IID.

oracle.label: function_value
oracle.details: Unbiased stochastic values of the entire constraint vector c at both requested points, jointly with the gradient and Jacobian estimates. Objective values are not supplied.

distinctive_assumptions.label: bounded_variance
distinctive_assumptions.details: The sum of expected squared errors of the objective gradient, constraint values, and Jacobian is uniformly at most σ². No exponential-tail assumption is imposed.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: E is a finite-dimensional real inner-product space; constraints lie in Euclidean m-space.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: Globally, ‖∇f(x)‖ and ‖J(x)‖ ≤ H, and both maps are H-Lipschitz. Uniform surjectivity requires ‖ℓ‖ ≤ H‖J(x)ᵀℓ‖ for every x and ℓ. The joint stochastic gradient/value/Jacobian map satisfies mean-square H-Lipschitz continuity under shared samples. The penalty f(x)+4H(H+1)∑ᵢ[cᵢ(x)]₊ has initial gap at most Δ. All Params are public, including x0, m, H, σ, Δ, ε; f, c, J and the sampling law are hidden. Validity requires m>0, H≥1, σ,Δ≥0 and 0<ε≤1.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/StochasticSurjectiveInequalities.lean: Regularity, penalty, OracleConditions.meanSquaredSmooth, spec.Public, spec.publicInput, spec.valid, spec.admissible.

accuracy.label: high_probability
accuracy.details: The output is measurable and all accuracy conditions hold jointly with probability at least 3/4 under a fixed oracle-call budget.

accuracy.label: other
accuracy.details: Output a primal-dual pair (x,ℓ) with ℓ≥0, Lagrangian stationarity ‖∇f(x)+J(x)ᵀℓ‖≤ε and absolute complementarity ∑ᵢ|ℓᵢcᵢ(x)|≤ε.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: The stochastic nonlinear-programming formulation combines global uniform Jacobian surjectivity, jointly mean-square smooth paired evaluations, a penalty-gap initialization bound, and simultaneous probabilistic stationarity, feasibility, and absolute complementarity requirements.

descriptionHtml:
Stochastic Surjective Inequality Constraints

We study minimizing a differentiable function f:E→R subject to differentiable inequalities ci(x)≤0, i=1,…,m, on a finite-dimensional real inner-product space E. Objective and constraint gradients are bounded and Lipschitz, the constraint derivative is uniformly surjective, and a given point has bounded initial penalty gap. Each oracle call returns unbiased stochastic objective gradients, constraint values, and constraint gradients at two points using one shared sample; successive samples are independent, with bounded variance and mean-square Lipschitz dependence on the points. For ε>0, the goal is a measurable pair (x¯,λ¯)∈E×Rm satisfying λ¯≥0, ∥∇f(x¯)+∑iλ¯i∇ci(x¯)∥≤ε, ∥(max{ci(x¯),0})i=1m∥2≤ε, and ∑i|λ¯ici(x¯)|≤ε simultaneously with probability at least 3/4.

The optimization problem is minx∈E: ci(x)≤0, i=1,…,mf(x). Write c=(c1,…,cm):E→Rm and J(x)=(∇ci(x))i=1m∈Em,J(x)⊤λ=∑i=1mλi∇ci(x). We use the inner-product norm on E, the Euclidean norm on Rm, and the product norm ∥A∥2=∑i=1m∥Ai∥2 on Em. In particular, all norms of J below are product norms. Fix m∈N,m≥1,H≥1,σ≥0,Δ≥0,0<ε≤1, and a given point x0∈E. The algorithm receives E, the measurable sample space Ω, and m,H,σ,Δ,ε,x0.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Regularity and surjectivity). The functions f and ci, i=1,…,m, are differentiable everywhere. For every x,y∈E, ∥∇f(x)∥≤H,∥J(x)∥≤H,∥∇f(x)−∇f(y)∥≤H∥x−y∥,∥J(x)−J(y)∥≤H∥x−y∥. Moreover, for every x∈E and λ∈Rm, ∥λ∥2≤H∥J(x)⊤λ∥.

Assumption 2 (Initial penalty gap). Define the penalty function Φ(x)=f(x)+4H(H+1)∑i=1mmax{ci(x),0}. The given point satisfies Φ(x0)−Φ(x)≤Δfor every x∈E.

Assumption 3 (Stochastic primitive estimates). There is a probability measure ν on Ω and jointly measurable maps g:E×Ω→E,v:E×Ω→Rm,D:E×Ω→Em. For each x∈E, these maps are Bochner integrable in their sample argument and satisfy Eξ∼ν[g(x,ξ)]=∇f(x),Eξ∼ν[v(x,ξ)]=c(x),Eξ∼ν[D(x,ξ)]=J(x). For every x,y∈E, the nonnegative random variables inside the following expectations are integrable, and Eξ∼ν[∥g(x,ξ)−∇f(x)∥2+∥v(x,ξ)−c(x)∥22+∥D(x,ξ)−J(x)∥2]≤σ2, Eξ∼ν[∥g(x,ξ)−g(y,ξ)∥2+∥v(x,ξ)−v(y,ξ)∥22+∥D(x,ξ)−D(y,ξ)∥2]≤H2∥x−y∥2.

A query is any pair (x,y)∈E×E. At call k, the oracle returns ((g(x,ξk),v(x,ξk),D(x,ξk)),(g(y,ξk),v(y,ξk),D(y,ξk))). The measurable samples (ξk)k≥0 are mutually independent with common law ν, and are independent of the algorithm’s randomness. Thus both points in one query share a sample, and each paired reply counts as one oracle call.

After the allotted calls, the output (x¯,λ¯) must be measurable. Under P, the joint law of the algorithm’s randomness and the sample sequence, the following conditions must hold simultaneously with probability at least 3/4: λ¯i≥0(i=1,…,m),∥∇f(x¯)+J(x¯)⊤λ¯∥≤ε,‖(max{ci(x¯),0})i=1m‖2≤ε,∑i=1m|λ¯ici(x¯)|≤ε.

comparisonHtml:
Minimize f(x) subject to c(x)≤0 in a finite-dimensional real inner-product space, with m≥1, H≥1, σ,Δ≥0, 0<ε≤1. Globally, ∥∇f∥,∥J∥F≤H, ∇f,J are H-Lipschitz, and ∥λ∥≤H∥J(x)⊤λ∥ for every x,λ. The penalty Φ=f+4H(H+1)∑i[ci]+ satisfies Φ(x0)−infΦ≤Δ. Jointly measurable, integrable oracle triples Z=(g,v,D) have mean (∇f,c,J), summed variance at most σ2, and ∫∥Z(x,ω)−Z(y,ω)∥2dp≤H2∥x−y∥2. Samples are IID with law p under probability law P; paired evaluations share a sample. Target: output (x,λ≥0) such that, with P-probability at least 3/4, ∥∇f(x)+J(x)⊤λ∥≤ε, ∥[c(x)]+∥≤ε, and ∑i|λici(x)|≤ε.

Stochastic nonlinear inequalities: StochasticSurjectiveInequalities.
Result Oracle complexity Novelty Limitations
(1) SurjectiveStochasticInequalityKkt (Ours) (⋆⋆⋆) (review) O(1+m2H10Δ+m4H18σ2ε2+m4H19Δσε3) evaluations of each primitive, including batches and paired calls.
(2) SARAH Gauss–Newton (Tran-Dinh et al. 2020), Thm. 4.3 Values: O(1+σ2/ε4+Δ/ε5); gradients/Jacobians: O(1+σ2/ε2+Δ/ε3). Fixed m,H; their polynomial factors are unquantified. Target: E∥G~M∥2≤ε2 for the hinge-penalty composite. (1): Value exponent ε−5→ε−3 for fixed m,H,σ,Δ>0 as ε→0; gradient/Jacobian exponent matched. Accuracy targets differ. (1) requires global surjectivity. Conversion of (2) to KKT accuracy is unestablished; no identical-target speedup asserted. Large proved constants can dominate at moderate accuracy.
(3) Recursive momentum (Shi and Wang 2025), Thm. 7; linear-slack subclass only Total O(ε−5(1+log⁡(1/ε))2), dominated by values; gradient/Jacobian cost O(ε−3(1+log⁡(1/ε))2). Other parameters fixed; confidence 1−ε. Requires Strong MFCQ, bounded noise, samplewise smoothness, bounded c and lower-bounded f on the iterate region. (1): On the common slack subclass, value exponent 5→3 as ε→0. Finite variance and mean-square smoothness replace bounded noise and samplewise smoothness; only penalty lower bound needed. (1) has fixed 3/4 confidence; (3) has 1−ε. Global all-row surjectivity is stronger than Strong MFCQ.
(4) SmALM (Cui et al. 2026), Thm. 4.2; equality constraints only O(ε−3) expected evaluations of each primitive, other parameters fixed; expected stochastic ε-KKT accuracy. Requires bounded c, lower-bounded f, uniform full rank and Lipschitz Hessians on the iterate region. (1) covers inequalities with C1,1 data; (4) treats equalities with Lipschitz ∇2f,∇2c. Rates are not comparable: no valid KKT-preserving reduction established. (1) does not cover (4)’s equality problems; replacing c=0 by ±c≤0 violates surjectivity.

Abbr: J is the constraint Jacobian; [c]+ is the componentwise positive part; ∥⋅∥F is the Frobenius norm. Product norms square-sum the three oracle errors. A primitive evaluation means one evaluation of g, v, or D; each paired query evaluates each twice. G~M is the stochastic prox-linear gradient mapping. IID means independent and identically distributed; KKT means Karush–Kuhn–Tucker; MFCQ means Mangasarian–Fromovitz constraint qualification.

Cui, Yawen, Qiankun Shi, Xiao Wang, and Xiantao Xiao. 2026. A Fletcher’s Augmented Lagrangian-Based Stochastic First-Order Method for Nonconvex Equality-Constrained Optimization. Optimization Online preprint. https://optimization-online.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/SmALM-5.pdf.

Nguyen. 2020. “Stochastic Gauss–Newton Algorithms for Nonconvex Compositional Optimization.” Proceedings of the 37th International Conference on Machine Learning, Proceedings of machine learning research, vol. 119: 9572–82. https://proceedings.mlr.press/v119/tran-dinh20a.html.

import LongTails.Template
import LongTails.Setups.StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Gradient.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.PiL2

open MeasureTheory
open scoped RealInnerProductSpace

namespace LongTails.Setups.StochasticSurjectiveInequalities

open OracleTemplate

structure Params where
  E : Type
  [normedE : NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [innerE : InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
  [finiteE : FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
  [measurableE : MeasurableSpace E]
  [borelE : BorelSpace E]
  Ω : Type
  [measurableΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω]
  m : ℕ
  H : ℝ
  σ : ℝ
  Δ : ℝ
  ε : ℝ
  x0 : E

attribute [instance] Params.normedE Params.innerE Params.finiteE Params.measurableE
  Params.borelE Params.measurableΩ

abbrev Constraint (p : Params) := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p.m)
abbrev Jacobian (p : Params) := PiLp 2 (fun _ : Fin p.m => p.E)
abbrev Primitive (p : Params) := p.E × Constraint p × Jacobian p

instance (p : Params) : MeasurableSpace (Constraint p) := borel (Constraint p)
instance (p : Params) : BorelSpace (Constraint p) := ⟨rfl⟩
instance (p : Params) : MeasurableSpace (Jacobian p) := borel (Jacobian p)
instance (p : Params) : BorelSpace (Jacobian p) := ⟨rfl⟩

structure Problem (p : Params) where
  f : p.E → ℝ
  c : p.E → Constraint p
  J : p.E → Jacobian p

def transposeAction (p : Params) (J : Jacobian p) (ℓ : Constraint p) : p.E :=
  ∑ i, ℓ i • J i

def penalty (p : Params) (I : Problem p) (x : p.E) : ℝ :=
  I.f x + 4 * p.H * (p.H + 1) * ∑ i, max (I.c x i) 0

structure Regularity (q : Params) (I : Problem q) : Prop where
  hasGradient : ∀ x, HasGradientAt I.f (gradient I.f x) x
  constraintGradient : ∀ x i, HasGradientAt (fun y => I.c y i) (I.J x i) x
  gradientBound : ∀ x, ‖gradient I.f x‖ ≤ q.H
  jacobianBound : ∀ x, ‖I.J x‖ ≤ q.H
  gradientLipschitz : ∀ x y, ‖gradient I.f x - gradient I.f y‖ ≤ q.H * ‖x - y‖
  jacobianLipschitz : ∀ x y, ‖I.J x - I.J y‖ ≤ q.H * ‖x - y‖
  surjective : ∀ x ℓ, ‖ℓ‖ ≤ q.H * ‖transposeAction q (I.J x) ℓ‖
  initialGap : ∀ x, penalty q I q.x0 - penalty q I x ≤ q.Δ

structure OracleConditions (q : Params) (I : Problem q)
    (g : q.E → q.Ω → q.E) (v : q.E → q.Ω → Constraint q)
    (D : q.E → q.Ω → Jacobian q) (p : ProbabilityMeasure q.Ω) : Prop where
  gradientMeasurable : Measurable (Function.uncurry g)
  valueMeasurable : Measurable (Function.uncurry v)
  jacobianMeasurable : Measurable (Function.uncurry D)
  integrable : ∀ x, Integrable (g x) p ∧ Integrable (v x) p ∧ Integrable (D x) p
  gradientMean : ∀ x, ∫ ω, g x ω ∂p = gradient I.f x
  valueMean : ∀ x, ∫ ω, v x ω ∂p = I.c x
  jacobianMean : ∀ x, ∫ ω, D x ω ∂p = I.J x
  varianceIntegrable : ∀ x, Integrable (fun ω => ‖g x ω - gradient I.f x‖ ^ 2 +
    ‖v x ω - I.c x‖ ^ 2 + ‖D x ω - I.J x‖ ^ 2) p
  variance : ∀ x, ∫ ω, (‖g x ω - gradient I.f x‖ ^ 2 +
    ‖v x ω - I.c x‖ ^ 2 + ‖D x ω - I.J x‖ ^ 2) ∂p ≤ q.σ ^ 2
  differenceIntegrable : ∀ x y, Integrable (fun ω => ‖g x ω - g y ω‖ ^ 2 +
    ‖v x ω - v y ω‖ ^ 2 + ‖D x ω - D y ω‖ ^ 2) p
  meanSquaredSmooth : ∀ x y, ∫ ω, (‖g x ω - g y ω‖ ^ 2 + ‖v x ω - v y ω‖ ^ 2 +
    ‖D x ω - D y ω‖ ^ 2) ∂p ≤ q.H ^ 2 * ‖x - y‖ ^ 2

def accurate (p : Params) (I : Problem p) (out : p.E × Constraint p) : Prop :=
  (∀ i, 0 ≤ out.2 i) ∧
  ‖gradient I.f out.1 + transposeAction p (I.J out.1) out.2‖ ≤ p.ε ∧
  ‖(WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => max (I.c out.1 i) 0) : Constraint p)‖ ≤ p.ε ∧
  ∑ i, |out.2 i * I.c out.1 i| ≤ p.ε

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Params
  Instance p := Problem p
  Query p := p.E × p.E
  Reply p := Primitive p × Primitive p
  Output p := p.E × Constraint p
  publicInput p := p
  valid p := 0 < p.m ∧ 1 ≤ p.H ∧ 0 ≤ p.σ ∧ 0 ≤ p.Δ ∧ 0 < p.ε ∧ p.ε ≤ 1
  admissible q I O :=
    ∃ (g : q.E → q.Ω → q.E) (v : q.E → q.Ω → Constraint q)
      (D : q.E → q.Ω → Jacobian q)
      (p : ProbabilityMeasure q.Ω) (P : ProbabilityMeasure (ℕ → q.Ω)),
      LongTails.Setups.StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex.IID
        (fun k (ξ : ℕ → q.Ω) => ξ k) (p : Measure _) (P : Measure _) ∧
      O = { Seed := fun _ => q.Ω
            law := P
            answer := fun _ (_, z) ω =>
              ((g z.1 ω, v z.1 ω, D z.1 ω), (g z.2 ω, v z.2 ω, D z.2 ω)) } ∧
      Regularity q I ∧ OracleConditions q I g v D p
  successful q I output P :=
    Measurable output ∧ ENNReal.ofReal (3 / 4) ≤ (P : Measure _) {ω | accurate q I (output ω)}

end LongTails.Setups.StochasticSurjectiveInequalities
